correctness.rationale: Independently differentiated V=(x-1)²+y²+(z+1)² along xdot=y+2xy+xz, ydot=1-2x²+yz, zdot=x-x²-y² with sympy, getting Vdot=-2q exactly, q=x²+xy+y²-x. Completing square q=(x-2/3)²+(x-2/3)(y+1/3)+(y+1/3)²-1/3 yields ellipse E with matrix [[1,1/2],[1/2,1]] and area 2pi/(3sqrt3). On a radius-R sphere, the two z-graphs exist over E for R>=2, normal velocity -q/R, area element R/sqrt(R²-rho²), so f_R=1/(2pi R²)int_E R/sqrt(R²-rho²), and J_R=2int_E(-q)/sqrt(R²-rho²). Exact ellipse integral int_E(-q)=pi/(9sqrt3) gives coefficients. Uniform expansion on bounded E establishes the claimed error orders. q>=-1/3 implies Vdot<=2/3 and forward nonexplosion; the reversing involution (x,-y,-z) verified symbolically gives backward nonexplosion and O(sqrt(1+|t|)). Integrating derivatives of V,z against compact invariant measures yields exactly E(xy)=0 and the shifted unit circle mean square 1/4. No global orbit boundedness or attractor existence is claimed.
residual_risks: Outward-pointing patches do not imply global orbit escape, and O(sqrt(1+|t|)) does NOT prove uniform boundedness as |t|→infinity; compact invariant measure equalities are conditional on its existence.

final_claim: For Sprott 2014 exact quadratic vector field, centered radius V^(1/2) about (1,0,-1), Vdot=-2(x²+xy+y²-x) identifies two outgoing graphs over a fixed ellipse for every R>=2. Area fraction f_R=1/(3sqrt3 R²)+O(R^-4), positive outward flux J_R=2pi/(9sqrt3 R)+O(R^-3); all maximal trajectories are complete in both time directions with at-most square-root-in-time norm growth; compact invariant probability measures satisfy E(xy)=0 and E((x-1/2)²+y²)=1/4.
